elements.element: Customer owns Deliverables and work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: Retained §13: "Garman is the owner of all intellectual property rights in the Work (including any Improvements or Modifications thereto)... No title to the intellectual property in the Work is transferred to Sparkling." Vendor, not Customer, owns the work product, including the Schedule "D" Modifications Customer pays for.

elements.element: Vendor assigns the Deliverables and work product to Customer.
elements.evidence: No assignment language anywhere in the rendered text; §13 expressly negates transfer of title to Sparkling.

elements.element: Vendor retains its pre-existing intellectual property.
elements.evidence: §13 retained unchanged: Garman owns all intellectual property rights in the Work and related materials, logos and names.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Vendor IP embedded in Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Rendered §2 grants "a perpetual... licence" to the Software (including Improvements and Modifications) and Documentation, and the new §17(a) sentence confirms the Section 2 licence survives expiry or termination.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: Rendered §2: "perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free... licence"; the fee/termination condition on the licence was removed from §17(a).

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: Rendered §2 states "royalty-free" and the additional-fees-for-other-locations sentence was deleted.

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: The inserted sentence only limits Garman's licence in Sparkling's data; no operative statement that Sparkling retains all right, title and interest in its data (including converted data under Schedule "D").

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: Inserted after §4(b): "Any licence granted to Garman in Sparkling's data is limited to processing that data solely to provide the services under this Agreement."

elements.element: The parties do not jointly own intellectual property.
elements.evidence: No joint-ownership language exists; §13 vests sole ownership of the Work in Garman and the redline creates only a licence in Customer's favour.

elements.element: Vendor may retain ownership of generic tools and know-how.
elements.evidence: Already met and preserved: §13 "Garman is the owner of all intellectual property rights in the Work (including any Improvements or Modifications thereto)..."

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Rendered §2: "a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, non-transferable and non-exclusive licence"; §17(a) now reads "The licence granted under Section 2 survives expiry or termination of this Agreement," removing the prior fee/termination contradiction.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: "irrevocable" appears in the rendered §2 grant, and the licence is no longer conditioned on continued fee payment or non-termination in §17(a).

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is worldwide.
elements.evidence: "worldwide" appears in the grant; the Authorized-Locations place-of-use cap and the additional-fee sentence for other locations were removed, so no retained sentence contradicts it.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: "royalty-free" in the grant; the sentence making use at other locations "subject to the payment of additional fees" was deleted.

elements.element: Customer may use and modify Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: Rendered §2: "licence to use, modify and sublicense for Sparkling's business purposes: (i) the Software, including any Improvements and Modifications... and (ii) the Documentation."

elements.element: Customer may sublicense Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: "sublicense for Sparkling's business purposes" in §2, and the conflicting bar in §3(c) ("or grant a sublicence of the Work") was deleted; only assign/transfer/lease/export restrictions remain.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: New sentence at §4(b): "Any licence granted to Garman in Sparkling's data is limited to processing that data solely to provide the services under this Agreement." This addresses the unrestricted use of converted data.

reasons: Fallback is position-complete: all eight fallback elements are met in operative language. Vendor ownership of the Work is untouched (§13), the Section 2 grant now carries perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide and royalty-free modifiers plus use, modify and sublicense rights for Sparkling's business, the Improvements/Modifications are brought inside the licensed scope, and the Customer-data processing limit is inserted at §4(b).

Preferred is not met: Vendor still owns the Deliverables/Work with no assignment to Customer (§13 retained verbatim), and there is no sentence confirming Customer retains all rights in its data. The finding is correctly targeted at the fallback rather than the preferred level.

Each deletion is necessary to the selected elements rather than cosmetic: the Authorized-Locations place-of-use cap and the additional-fee sentence directly contradict "worldwide" and "royalty-free"; the §3(c) sublicence bar contradicts the sublicense element; and the §17(a) fee/termination condition on the licence contradicts "perpetual" and "irrevocable". Customer-favourable retained language ("non-transferable", non-exclusive, affiliate coverage, the AS400 object-code delivery wording, and the rest of §3(c)) survives.

The §17(a) survival sentence is not a gratuitous survival tail; without it the retained "as long as fees are paid... and the Agreement is not otherwise terminated" language would leave the perpetual/irrevocable elements internally inconsistent. The cross-reference to Section 2 matches the amended grant clause.

No new dangling or undefined terms are created: "the services under this Agreement" is used descriptively, not as an undefined capitalised defined term, and no assignment of Customer IP or data to Vendor is introduced, so the walk-away line is not crossed.

Drafting improvement (not a completeness failure at fallback): if the team also wants the preferred position, add an express sentence that Sparkling retains all right, title and interest in Sparkling data (including data converted under Schedule "D"), and check that the Fee Schedule does not separately price per-location use in a way that undercuts the new royalty-free/worldwide grant.
